task.title: Clip, mask and blend
task.shortdesc: You can show only a part of an element, fade it with a mask, and choose how it mixes with what is behind it. The chapter Shadows, opacity, transforms and masks explains each effect in full.

info.p: A clip cuts away the parts of an element outside an area. You define the area with a clipPath element or with a basic shape, and you name it in the clip-path property. Clip elements describes the shapes, the reference boxes and the units.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <clipPath id="disc"> <circle cx="55" cy="45" r="32"/> </clipPath> </defs> <rect x="10" y="10" width="90" height="70" fill="#cfe3f5" clip-path="url(#disc)"/>

step.cmd: Fade an element with a mask

info.p: A mask makes parts of an element transparent. You define it with a mask element and you name it in the mask property or attribute. Where the mask is light the element shows, and where it is dark the element is transparent. Mask elements describes the type, the region, the units and the layers of a mask.

stepxmp.pre: <defs> <linearGradient id="ramp"> <stop offset="0" stop-color="#ffffff"/> <stop offset="1" stop-color="#000000"/> </linearGradient> <mask id="fade-out"> <rect x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="url(#ramp)"/> </mask> </defs> <rect x="120" y="10" width="95" height="70" fill="#1d4f7a" mask="url(#fade-out)"/>

step.cmd: Blend an element with what is behind it

info.p: The mix-blend-mode property chooses how the colors of an element mix with the colors under it, and isolation: isolate keeps a group from blending with what is outside it. Blend elements lists the modes.

fig.title: A clip, a mask and a blend mode

image.alt: A light blue disc cut from a rectangle. A dark blue rectangle that fades from opaque on the left to transparent on the right. Two overlapping circles, blue and yellow, whose overlap is green.

stepxmp.pre: <circle cx="260" cy="45" r="28" fill="#6fc3e8"/> <circle cx="285" cy="45" r="28" fill="#f2d649" style="mix-blend-mode: multiply"/>
